newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Boesak charged with theft of aid funds.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Boesak charged with theft of aid funds.

text.p: Anti-apartheid cleric and former World Council of Reformed Churches leader Allan Boesak was charged in absentia on Friday with fraud and theft from Western aid agencies.
State prosecutor Steven Powell told Reuters that Boesak, who is living in the United States, and former bookkeeper Freddie Steenkamp faced nine counts of fraud and 21 counts of theft.
"We are arranging the (court) appearance of Dr Boesak. His lawyers have told us he will be coming back on his own accord," he said.

Boesak, who headed the anti-apartheid Foundation for Peace and Justice, has been under investigation for more than two years concerning the disappearance or misuse of mainly Danish and Swedish aid funds totalling close to two million rand ($422,000).
"The fraud charge relates to different projects the foundation had...The amount involved is just over a million rand in respect of each of them (Boesak and Steenkamp)," Powell said.
Steenkamp faced the same charges in the Cape Town magistrates' court on Friday and was released on bail of 2,000 rand. He had to surrender his passport and must report to police each Sunday.
Boesak and Anglican Archbishop Desmond Tutu led the black struggle against apartheid during five years of emergency rule, which saw thousands of black opposition activists jailed without charge.
The case was adjourned to January 17 next year.
